To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the structure of the catalytic subunit complexed with the peptide inhibitor, PKl(5-24) is an open conformation and the structure determination of this binary complex is a demonstration that considerable information about the structure can be obtained from a partial model.

the crystal structures of binary complexes of the catalytic subunit (C) of cAMP-dependent (cAMP-DP) protein kinase with the peptide inhibitor PKI(5,24) and with the peptide inhibitor peptide PKI(5(6),24) differ from each other in a way that can be understood as a result of the difference in the number of positively charged residues on the peptide inhibitors.

the structure of the porcines heart catalytic subunit (C) of cAMP-dependent kinase complexed with an inhibitor peptide, PKI(6-24) (di-iodinated), crystallized in a new space group, P4(1)(2)1, and that the small lobe, which is closed in the previously determined crystal structure of a similar binary complex, is now open.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the molecular mechanism of the catalytic subunit by determining its three-dimensional structures at atomic resolution in various ligand-bound and ligand-free conformations.
the structure and function of the catalytic subunit (C) of cAMP-dependent (PKA) protein kinase.
a detailed understanding of the structural and functional properties of cAMP-dependent kinase and its role in the control of cell function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the two crystal structures are similar, but not identical, and that the two structures are not isomorphous.
the two binary complex structures are essentially the same, but the cubic crystal is open and the orthorhobomic crystal is closed.

the crystal structure of the binary complex of the catalytic subunit and PKI(5--24) is similar in overall conformation to that of the binary complex between the catalytic subunits and a peptide inhibitor of the recombinants.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the crystal structure of the catalytic subunit is a complex mixture of open and closed conformational states.
the crystallographic R-factor is a measure of the quality of the electron density map and not a measure of the accuracy of the atomic positions.

the structure of the catalytic subunit is very similar to the structure of the recombinantly produced mouse enzyme and that the small lobe undergoes significant conformational changes in different binary complexes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the crystal structure of a complex between the C subunit of cAPK and the inhibitor peptide PKI(5–24) is a closed conformation and that the structure of the same complex with a single mutation of the inhibitor peptide is an open conformation, which has implications for the mechanism of cAPK activation.
it is possible to obtain useful information from electron density maps even when the crystal structure is not complete.
the small and large lobe of the catalytic subunit are flexible and that this flexibility is likely important for the catalytic activity of the enzyme.
